claim: daf-7 encodes a TGFβ family neuroendocrine ligand that regulates diverse aspects of C. elegans behavior and physiology.
source: daf-7, which encodes a TGFβ family neuroendocrine ligand that regulates diverse aspects of C. elegans behavior and physiology (Chang et al., 2006; Fletcher and Kim, 2017; Gallagher et al., 2013; Greer et al., 2008; Milward et al., 2011; Ren et al., 1996; Shaw et al., 2007; White and Jorgensen, 2012; You et al., 2008)
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior published work establishing daf-7's identity and function.

claim: daf-7 is expressed in a sex-specific and context-dependent manner in the sex-shared ASJ chemosensory neurons.
source: daf-7, which encodes a TGFβ family neuroendocrine ligand that regulates diverse aspects of C. elegans behavior and physiology (Chang et al., 2006; Fletcher and Kim, 2017; Gallagher et al., 2013; Greer et al., 2008; Milward et al., 2011; Ren et al., 1996; Shaw et al., 2007; White and Jorgensen, 2012; You et al., 2008), is expressed in a sex-specific and context-dependent manner in the sex-shared ASJ chemosensory neurons
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Hilbert and Kim, 2017; Meisel et al., 2014) that established this expression pattern.

claim: daf-7 expression in ASJ functions to promote exploratory behaviors.
source: is expressed in a sex-specific and context-dependent manner in the sex-shared ASJ chemosensory neurons and functions to promote exploratory behaviors (Hilbert and Kim, 2017; Meisel et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Regulation of daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons requires the integration of sensory and internal state information including the sex and age of the animal, its nutritional state, and the type of bacterial species it encounters.
source: Regulation of daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons requires the integration of sensory and internal state information including the sex and age of the animal, its nutritional state, and the type of bacterial species it encounters in its environment (Hilbert and Kim, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: PDF-1 pathway signaling is essential for male mate-searching behavior.
source: We show that PDF-1 pathway signaling, which has previously been shown to be essential for male mate-searching behavior (Barrios et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior published work.

claim: Males with mutation of the PDF-1 neuropeptide ligand have markedly attenuated expression of daf-7 in the ASJ neuron pair.
source: We observed that males with mutation of either the PDF-1 neuropeptide ligand or its receptor, PDFR-1, have markedly attenuated expression of daf-7 in the ASJ neuron pair (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B measuring daf-7 expression in mutant males.

claim: Males with mutation of the PDFR-1 receptor have markedly attenuated expression of daf-7 in the ASJ neuron pair.
source: We observed that males with mutation of either the PDF-1 neuropeptide ligand or its receptor, PDFR-1, have markedly attenuated expression of daf-7 in the ASJ neuron pair (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B measuring daf-7 expression in mutant males.

claim: In PDF-1 pathway mutant males, there is no difference in daf-7 levels in the ASI neurons when compared to wild-type.
source: In the PDF-1 pathway mutant males, we observe no difference in daf-7 levels in the ASI neurons when compared to WT (Figure 1C)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C comparing daf-7 expression in ASI neurons.

claim: The PDF-1 pathway specifically affects the regulation of daf-7 in the ASJ neuron pair.
source: In the PDF-1 pathway mutant males, we observe no difference in daf-7 levels in the ASI neurons when compared to WT (Figure 1C), suggesting that the PDF-1 pathway specifically affects the regulation of daf-7 in the ASJ neuron pair.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that PDF-1 pathway mutations affect daf-7 in ASJ but not ASI neurons.

claim: The ASI chemosensory neurons are established sites of daf-7 expression in both male and hermaphrodite animals.
source: The ASI chemosensory neurons are established sites of daf-7 expression in both male and hermaphrodite animals (Ren et al., 1996; Schackwitz et al., 1996)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Expression of daf-7 in the ASJ neuron pair of males is required for the male-specific mate-searching behavioral program.
source: Expression of daf-7 in the ASJ neuron pair of males is required for the male-specific mate-searching behavioral program (Hilbert and Kim, 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior published work.

claim: Overexpression of the pdf-1 genomic sequence confers increased mate-searching behavior in male animals.
source: Overexpression of the pdf-1 genomic sequence confers increased mate-searching behavior in male animals (Figure 1D; Barrios et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and citation to prior work.

claim: The effect of PDF-1 overexpression on mate-searching behavior is suppressed by loss of daf-7 function.
source: We introduced a daf-7 mutation into these transgenic PDF-1 overexpressing lines and observed that the effect of PDF-1 overexpression on mate-searching behavior was suppressed by loss of daf-7 function (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Overexpression of daf-7 in the ASJ neurons of pdf-1(tm1996) mutant males cannot rescue the mate-searching defects of these animals.
source: However, we observed that overexpression of daf-7 in the ASJ neurons of pdf-1(tm1996) mutant males could not rescue the mate-searching defects of these animals (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: PDF-1 regulates mate-searching behavior in males through the regulation of daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons and through additional mechanisms functioning in parallel to DAF-7 signaling.
source: Taken together, the results of this epistasis analysis suggest that PDF-1 regulates mate-searching behavior in males through the regulation of daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons and through additional mechanisms functioning in parallel to DAF-7 signaling.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the epistasis analysis showing that PDF-1 overexpression requires daf-7, but daf-7 overexpression cannot rescue pdf-1 mutants.

claim: daf-7 expression is induced by the presence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in both sexes to promote pathogen avoidance behaviors.
source: We have previously reported that daf-7 expression serves a dual role in the ASJ neurons, functioning in males to promote food-leaving behaviors (Hilbert and Kim, 2017), but also being induced by the presence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in both sexes to promote pathogen avoidance behaviors (Meisel et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: PDF-1 signaling is not required for the upregulation of daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons after 16 hr on P. aeruginosa in hermaphrodites.
source: We did not observe a requirement for PDF-1 signaling in the induction of daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons after 16 hr on P. aeruginosa; both pdf-1 and pdfr-1 mutant hermaphrodites had equivalent levels of daf-7 expression when compared to control animals (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E comparing daf-7 expression in mutant and control hermaphrodites on P. aeruginosa.

claim: Males that are mutant for either the PDF-1 ligand or receptor are capable of upregulating daf-7 expression in ASJ upon exposure to P. aeruginosa.
source: Similarly, males that are mutant for either the PDF-1 ligand or receptor (and show little to no daf-7 expression in their ASJ neurons on E. coli, see Figure 1B) were capable of upregulating daf-7 expression in ASJ upon exposure to P. aeruginosa (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: daf-7 mutant hermaphrodites fail to avoid a lawn of pathogenic P. aeruginosa.
source: Consistent with this expectation, we observed that while daf-7 mutant hermaphrodites fail to avoid a lawn of pathogenic bacteria, the pdf-1 and pdfr-1 mutant hermaphrodites appear wild-type for their ability to perform this behavior (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F measuring pathogen avoidance behavior.

claim: pdf-1 and pdfr-1 mutant hermaphrodites appear wild-type for their ability to avoid a lawn of pathogenic P. aeruginosa.
source: Consistent with this expectation, we observed that while daf-7 mutant hermaphrodites fail to avoid a lawn of pathogenic bacteria, the pdf-1 and pdfr-1 mutant hermaphrodites appear wild-type for their ability to perform this behavior (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F measuring pathogen avoidance behavior.

claim: pdf-1 and pdfr-1 mutant males display robust pathogen avoidance despite their defects in the male-specific mate searching behavior.
source: Similarly, pdf-1 and pdfr-1 mutant males also displayed robust pathogen avoidance despite their defects in the male-specific mate searching behavior (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B; Barrios et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and citation to prior work.

claim: The PDF-1 signaling pathway acts sex-specifically to regulate daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons and its effects on downstream sexually dimorphic behavioral programs.
source: These data suggest that the PDF-1 signaling pathway acts sex-specifically to regulate daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons and its effects on downstream sexually dimorphic behavioral programs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that PDF-1 pathway is required for male-specific daf-7 expression and mate-searching but not for pathogen avoidance in either sex.

claim: The PDF-1 neuropeptide ligand is secreted from multiple neurons in the head region of the animal.
source: The PDF-1 neuropeptide ligand is secreted from multiple neurons in the head region of the animal where a similarly large number of neurons express the PDFR-1 receptor (Barrios et al., 2012; Janssen et al., 2009; Meelkop et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: A large number of neurons express the PDFR-1 receptor in the head region of C. elegans.
source: The PDF-1 neuropeptide ligand is secreted from multiple neurons in the head region of the animal where a similarly large number of neurons express the PDFR-1 receptor (Barrios et al., 2012; Janssen et al., 2009; Meelkop et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Introduction of a genomic DNA fragment carrying the pdfr-1 locus fully rescues daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons of pdfr-1 mutant males.
source: We observed that while the pdfr-1 mutant males lack daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons, introduction of a genomic DNA fragment carrying the pdfr-1 locus fully rescued this phenotype and restored daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Expression of pdfr-1 under the control of the ASJ-specific trx-1 promoter is sufficient to rescue daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons of pdfr-1 mutant male animals.
source: Furthermore, we observed that expression of pdfr-1 under the control of the ASJ-specific trx-1 promoter was sufficient to rescue daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons of the mutant male animals, suggesting that PDF-1 signals to its receptor, PDFR-1, in the ASJ neurons to influence daf-7 expression specifically in the male (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: PDF-1 signals to its receptor, PDFR-1, in the ASJ neurons to influence daf-7 expression specifically in the male.
source: Furthermore, we observed that expression of pdfr-1 under the control of the ASJ-specific trx-1 promoter was sufficient to rescue daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons of the mutant male animals, suggesting that PDF-1 signals to its receptor, PDFR-1, in the ASJ neurons to influence daf-7 expression specifically in the male (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that ASJ-specific expression of pdfr-1 is sufficient to rescue daf-7 expression.

claim: Animals with ASJ-specific RNAi targeting pdfr-1 exhibit reduced daf-7 expression in ASJ.
source: We observed that animals with RNAi targeting pdfr-1 in the ASJ neurons exhibited reduced daf-7 expression in ASJ comparable to what we observed with ASJ-specific RNAi of GFP, our positive control (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: ASJ-specific expression of Cre recombinase suppresses the rescuing effects of a floxed pdfr-1 transgene on daf-7 expression.
source: We observed that this construct partially rescued daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons of pdfr-1(ok3425) mutant males, and ASJ-specific expression of the Cre recombinase suppressed the rescuing effects of this transgene (Figure 2D)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: PDFR-1 activity in the ASJ neurons is required for daf-7 expression.
source: We observed that this construct partially rescued daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons of pdfr-1(ok3425) mutant males, and ASJ-specific expression of the Cre recombinase suppressed the rescuing effects of this transgene (Figure 2D), strongly suggestive that PDFR-1 activity in the ASJ neurons is required for daf-7 expression.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the Cre-lox experiment showing that removal of pdfr-1 specifically in ASJ eliminates daf-7 expression.

claim: The PDF-1 signaling pathway functions cell-autonomously in the ASJ neuron pair to regulate the sexually dimorphic expression of daf-7.
source: These results indicate that the PDF-1 signaling pathway functions cell-autonomously in the ASJ neuron pair to regulate the sexually dimorphic expression of daf-7.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple experiments showing that pdfr-1 expression and activity specifically in ASJ is both necessary and sufficient for daf-7 expression.

claim: The PDFR-1 receptor is a secretin-family G-protein coupled receptor (GPCR).
source: The PDFR-1 receptor is a secretin-family G-protein coupled receptor (GPCR), which has been shown to stimulate Gαs signaling and upregulation of cAMP production in transfected cells as well as in both Drosophila melanogaster and C. elegans neurons (Figure 1A; Flavell et al., 2013; Hyun et al., 2005; Janssen et al., 2008; Lear et al., 2005; Mertens et al., 2005; Shafer et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work and established scientific knowledge.

claim: PDFR-1 stimulates Gαs signaling and upregulation of cAMP production in transfected cells as well as in both Drosophila melanogaster and C. elegans neurons.
source: The PDFR-1 receptor is a secretin-family G-protein coupled receptor (GPCR), which has been shown to stimulate Gαs signaling and upregulation of cAMP production in transfected cells as well as in both Drosophila melanogaster and C. elegans neurons (Figure 1A; Flavell et al., 2013; Hyun et al., 2005; Janssen et al., 2008; Lear et al., 2005; Mertens et al., 2005; Shafer et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: In pdfr-1 mutant males with transgenic expression of the acy-1(gf) cDNA only in the ASJ neurons, daf-7 expression is fully rescued.
source: We observed that in pdfr-1 mutant males with transgenic expression of the acy-1(gf) cDNA only in the ASJ neurons, daf-7 expression was fully rescued (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The PDF-1 signaling pathway acts directly on the ASJ neurons in order to regulate daf-7 expression in male animals.
source: This ability to bypass PDFR-1 by activation of cAMP production specifically in the ASJ neuron pair further suggest that the PDF-1 signaling pathway acts directly on the ASJ neurons in order to regulate daf-7 expression in male animals.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that activating the downstream signaling component (ACY-1) in ASJ can bypass the need for PDFR-1.

claim: Starvation of adult male animals efficiently suppresses daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons in wild-type animals.
source: We previously reported that starvation of adult male animals efficiently suppresses daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons in wild-type animals (Hilbert and Kim, 2017; Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work and experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: ASJ-specific expression of the acy-1(gf) variant in starved males does not suppress the effects of starvation on daf-7 expression in ASJ.
source: Notably, ASJ-specific expression of the acy-1(gf) variant in starved males did not suppress the effects of starvation on daf-7 expression in ASJ (Figure 3B)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The effects of starvation on daf-7 expression act downstream of or in parallel to PDFR-1-ACY-1 signaling.
source: Notably, ASJ-specific expression of the acy-1(gf) variant in starved males did not suppress the effects of starvation on daf-7 expression in ASJ (Figure 3B), suggestive that the effects of starvation act downstream of or in parallel to PDFR-1-ACY-1 signaling.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that constitutive activation of ACY-1 cannot overcome starvation-induced suppression of daf-7.

claim: pdf-1 is produced by the male-specific MCM neurons and is required for the regulation of sex-specific learning in males.
source: It was recently shown that pdf-1 is produced by the newly identified male-specific MCM neurons and is required for the regulation of sex-specific learning in males, but interestingly, ablation of these neurons has no effect on mate-searching behavior (Sammut et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior published work.

claim: Ablation of the male-specific MCM neurons has no effect on mate-searching behavior.
source: It was recently shown that pdf-1 is produced by the newly identified male-specific MCM neurons and is required for the regulation of sex-specific learning in males, but interestingly, ablation of these neurons has no effect on mate-searching behavior (Sammut et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior published work.

claim: Hermaphrodite animals carrying ASJ-expressed acy-1(gf) transgene show significant upregulation of daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons.
source: We first looked at hermaphrodite animals carrying the same ASJ-expressed acy-1(gf) transgene and observed significant upregulation of daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons of these hermaphrodites (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: In hermaphrodites with overexpression of pdfr-1 cDNA in the ASJ neurons, daf-7 expression is upregulated.
source: Strikingly, we found that in hermaphrodites with overexpression of pdfr-1 cDNA in the ASJ neurons, daf-7 expression was also upregulated similar to what we observed in the acy-1(gf) transgenic strains (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Hermaphrodites carrying the genomic pdfr-1 fragment with all of the endogenous regulatory sequence show no upregulation of daf-7 expression in ASJ.
source: We also quantified daf-7 expression in the ASJ neurons of hermaphrodites carrying the genomic pdfr-1 fragment with all of the endogenous regulatory sequence and observed no upregulation of expression in those animals.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing different pdfr-1 constructs.

claim: daf-7 expression in ASJ cannot be triggered simply as the result of overexpression of pdfr-1.
source: This control suggests that daf-7 expression in ASJ cannot be triggered simply as the result of overexpression of pdfr-1 (Figure 4B)
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that genomic pdfr-1 (with endogenous regulatory sequences) does not induce daf-7 in hermaphrodites, while heterologous overexpression does.

claim: Expression of PDFR-1 specifically in the hermaphrodite ASJ neurons is sufficient to allow daf-7 expression in these neurons.
source: rather, these results suggest that expression of PDFR-1 specifically in the hermaphrodite ASJ neurons is sufficient to allow daf-7 expression in these neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that heterologous expression of pdfr-1 in hermaphrodite ASJ induces daf-7 expression.

claim: Establishing the neuronal expression pattern of pdfr-1 has been challenging because of the apparent complexity of defining putative regulatory regions of the gene.
source: We note that establishing the neuronal expression pattern of pdfr-1 has been challenging because of the apparent complexity of defining putative regulatory regions of the gene (Barrios et al., 2012; Flavell et al., 2013; Janssen et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work that encountered these challenges.

claim: pdfr-1 mRNA shows a diffuse expression pattern with fluorescent signal observable in muscle tissue as well as in neurons.
source: Imaging of pdfr-1 transcription in WT animals revealed a diffuse expression pattern with fluorescent signal observable in muscle tissue as well as in neurons, but with few cells having strong signal and many cells with only scattered fluorescent spots, including the ASJ neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence in situ hybridization shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Puncta of pdfr-1 mRNA are observed in the ASJ neurons of about 20% of adult male animals.
source: We observed puncta of pdfr-1 mRNA in the ASJ neurons of about 20% of adult male animals (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and F)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence in situ hybridization shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: Similarly aged hermaphrodites do not have a corresponding subpopulation of animals with puncta of pdfr-1 mRNA in ASJ.
source: We observed puncta of pdfr-1 mRNA in the ASJ neurons of about 20% of adult male animals (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and F), whereas similarly aged hermaphrodites did not have a corresponding subpopulation of animals with puncta of pdfr-1 mRNA.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence in situ hybridization comparing males and hermaphrodites.

claim: PDFR-1 expression in the ASJ neurons is both necessary and sufficient for daf-7 expression.
source: Nevertheless, our functional studies demonstrating that PDFR-1 expression in the ASJ neurons is both necessary and sufficient for daf-7 expression suggest that the expression or activity of the PDFR-1 receptor may be regulated in a sexually dimorphic manner in these neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of rescue and knockdown experiments.

claim: The expression or activity of the PDFR-1 receptor may be regulated in a sexually dimorphic manner in the ASJ neurons.
source: Nevertheless, our functional studies demonstrating that PDFR-1 expression in the ASJ neurons is both necessary and sufficient for daf-7 expression suggest that the expression or activity of the PDFR-1 receptor may be regulated in a sexually dimorphic manner in these neurons.
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from functional studies and the sex-specific effects of the pathway.

claim: PDF signaling has a critical role in the regulation of circadian rhythmicity in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: In Drosophila melanogaster, PDF signaling has been well studied for its critical role in the regulation of circadian rhythmicity (Helfrich-Förster, 1995; Park and Hall, 1998; Park et al., 2000; Renn et al., 1999)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: PDF signaling modulates geotaxis in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: but it has also been shown to modulate geotaxis (Mertens et al., 2005), pheromone production and mating behaviors (Fujii and Amrein, 2010; Kim et al., 2013; Krupp et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: PDF signaling modulates pheromone production and mating behaviors in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: but it has also been shown to modulate geotaxis (Mertens et al., 2005), pheromone production and mating behaviors (Fujii and Amrein, 2010; Kim et al., 2013; Krupp et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: PDF-1 signaling is an important regulator of locomotion, roaming behaviors, quiescence, and male mate-searching behavior in C. elegans.
source: In C. elegans, PDF-1 signaling has been established as an important regulator of locomotion, roaming behaviors, quiescence, and notably, male mate-searching behavior (Figure 1A; Barrios et al., 2012; Choi et al., 2013; Flavell et al., 2013; Janssen et al., 2008, 2009; Meelkop et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The PDF neuropeptide signaling pathway is conserved among insects, crustaceans and nematodes.
source: The PDF neuropeptide signaling pathway is conserved among insects, crustaceans and nematodes.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about the conservation of this pathway.

claim: Sex-specific expression of daf-7 is regulated by the neuroendocrine ligand PDF-1.
source: Building on our previous work which described the sexually dimorphic expression of a neuroendocrine ligand, DAF-7, and its role in behavioral decision-making in C. elegans (Hilbert and Kim, 2017), we show here that sex-specific expression of daf-7 is regulated by another neuroendocrine ligand, Pigment Dispersing Factor (PDF-1)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: PDF-1 signaling acts sex- and cell-specifically in the ASJ neurons to regulate the expression of daf-7.
source: Our analysis revealed that PDF-1 signaling acts sex- and cell-specifically in the ASJ neurons to regulate the expression of daf-7
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Differences in PDFR-1 receptor activity account for the sex-specific effects of the PDF-1 pathway.
source: and we show that differences in PDFR-1 receptor activity account for the sex-specific effects of this pathway.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that heterologous expression of PDFR-1 in hermaphrodite ASJ induces daf-7 expression.

claim: Modulation of the sex-shared nervous system by a cascade of neuroendocrine signals can shape sexually dimorphic behaviors.
source: Our data suggest that modulation of the sex-shared nervous system by a cascade of neuroendocrine signals can shape sexually dimorphic behaviors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the overall findings of the study showing PDF-1 regulates DAF-7 to control sex-specific behaviors.

claim: The functional circuits for both male- and female-specific behaviors such as courtship and aggression are intact in the brains of both sexes in mice and are modulated by VNO activity in response to pheromone cues.
source: Studies of the mouse vomeronasal organ (VNO) has suggested that the functional circuits for both male- and female-specific behaviors such as courtship and aggression are intact in the brains of both sexes and are modulated by VNO activity in response to pheromone cues (Kimchi et al., 2007; Stowers et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The Drosophila male pheromone 11-cis Vaccenyl acetate (cVa) is sensed by the same neurons in the two sexes but stimulates distinct sex-specific behavioral responses.
source: In a similar vein, the Drosophila male pheromone 11-cis Vaccenyl acetate (cVa) has been shown to be sensed by the same neurons in the two sexes but stimulates distinct sex-specific behavioral responses (Datta et al., 2008; Kohl et al., 2013; Kurtovic et al., 2007; Ruta et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: C. elegans has two sexes: hermaphrodites and males.
source: In the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans, behavioral differences between the two sexes—hermaphrodites and males—
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about C. elegans biology.

claim: Egg laying is exclusively performed by hermaphrodites in C. elegans.
source: range from behaviors exclusively performed by one sex, such as egg laying by hermaphrodites and the mating program of males (Liu and Sternberg, 1995)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior published work and established knowledge.

claim: The mating program is exclusively performed by males in C. elegans.
source: range from behaviors exclusively performed by one sex, such as egg laying by hermaphrodites and the mating program of males (Liu and Sternberg, 1995)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior published work and established knowledge.

claim: The two sexes of C. elegans differ in their responses to pheromone.
source: to those in which the two sexes differ in their responses to the same stimuli, including differing responses to pheromone (Fagan et al., 2018; Jang et al., 2012; Srinivasan et al., 2008)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The two sexes of C. elegans differ in their responses to food-related cues.
source: including differing responses to pheromone (Fagan et al., 2018; Jang et al., 2012; Srinivasan et al., 2008), food-related cues (Ryan et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The two sexes of C. elegans differ in their responses to conditioning to aversive stimuli.
source: and conditioning to aversive stimuli (Sakai et al., 2013; Sammut et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The 294 neurons that are common to the nervous systems of both hermaphrodites and males have emerged as major contributors to a number of different sexually dimorphic behaviors.
source: While sex-specific neurons regulate corresponding behaviors in C. elegans, the 294 neurons that are common to the nervous systems of both hermaphrodites and males have emerged as major contributors to a number of different sexually dimorphic behaviors (Barr et al., 2018; Barrios et al., 2012, 2008; Fagan et al., 2018; Lee and Portman, 2007; Mowrey et al., 2014; Sakai et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Recent work has uncovered sexually dimorphic differences in axonic and dendritic morphology and synaptic connectivity within the sex shared nervous system of C. elegans.
source: In particular, recent work has uncovered sexually dimorphic differences in axonic and dendritic morphology and synaptic connectivity within the sex shared nervous system, which can modulate neuronal circuits and behavior (Hart and Hobert, 2018; Oren-Suissa et al., 2016; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2017a; Weinberg et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Sexual differentiation of neurons within the sex-shared nervous system of C. elegans is critical for the establishment of sexually dimorphic behaviors.
source: In addition, studies of sexually dimorphic gene expression (Hilbert and Kim, 2017; Ryan et al., 2014; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2017a) and neurotransmitter identity (Gendrel et al., 2016; Pereira et al., 2015; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2017a, 2017b) have suggested that sexual differentiation of neurons within the sex-shared nervous system of C. elegans is critical for the establishment of sexually dimorphic behaviors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from studies of sexually dimorphic gene expression and neurotransmitter identity cited.

claim: The neuromodulator oxytocin facilitates sex-specific social preference in male mice by modulating the ability of subsets of neurons to respond to social cues.
source: Interestingly, recent work in mice has uncovered a similar phenomenon wherein the neuromodulator oxytocin facilitates sex-specific social preference in male mice by modulating the ability of subsets of neurons to respond to social cues (Yao et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior published work.

claim: Sexually dimorphic regulation of the PDF-1 receptor, PDFR-1, may serve as a gating mechanism, allowing the ASJ neurons of adult male C. elegans to respond to the PDF-1 ligand.
source: Our data suggest that sexually dimorphic regulation of the PDF-1 receptor, PDFR-1, may serve as a gating mechanism, allowing the ASJ neurons of adult male C. elegans to respond to the PDF-1 ligand.
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from the experimental data showing sex-specific effects of PDFR-1.

claim: The PDF-1-PDFR-1 ligand-receptor interaction activates a downstream signaling cascade in ASJ terminating in the transcriptional activation of daf-7, which in turn promotes male-specific decision-making behaviors.
source: We suggest that this ligand-receptor interaction activates a downstream signaling cascade in ASJ terminating in the transcriptional activation of daf-7, which in turn promotes male-specific decision-making behaviors (Figure 4C, left).
evidence: The claim is a model inferred from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The relative lack of expression or activity of pdfr-1 in the hermaphrodite ASJ neurons prevents the activation of the PDF-1 pathway and consequently daf-7 expression is not induced under normal growth conditions in adult hermaphrodites.
source: We hypothesize that the relative lack of expression or activity of pdfr-1 in the hermaphrodite ASJ neurons prevents the activation of this pathway and consequently daf-7 expression is not induced under normal growth conditions in adult hermaphrodites (Figure 4C, right).
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis based on the experimental observations.

claim: Heterologous expression of the PDF-1 receptor in the hermaphrodite ASJ neurons is sufficient to drive daf-7 expression in an inappropriate physiological context.
source: Strikingly, heterologous expression of the PDF-1 receptor in the hermaphrodite ASJ neurons was sufficient to drive daf-7 expression in an inappropriate physiological context (the hermaphrodite nervous system).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that overexpression of pdfr-1 in hermaphrodite ASJ induces daf-7 expression.

claim: The PDF-1 pathway plays an integral role in facilitating sex-specific differences in gene expression and behavior.
source: All together, our data suggest that the PDF-1 pathway plays an integral role in facilitating sex-specific differences in gene expression and behavior.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the overall findings of the study.

claim: Two pathways, the PDF-1 and DAF-7/TGFβ pathways, act in concert as a neuroendocrine signaling cascade to regulate sex-specific behavior within the context of the sex-shared ASJ neurons.
source: Here, we propose a model in which two pathways, the PDF-1 and DAF-7/TGFβ pathways, act in concert as a neuroendocrine signaling cascade to regulate sex-specific behavior within the context of the sex-shared ASJ neurons (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is a model proposed based on the experimental findings.

claim: The PDF-1 pathway functions in tuning the response of the ASJ neurons to this endogenous neuromodulator in a sex-specific manner.
source: Our data suggest that the PDF-1 pathway functions in tuning the response of the ASJ neurons to this endogenous neuromodulator in a sex-specific manner.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing sex-specific effects of PDF-1 signaling.
